Before that, one important semantic bug: In `flowReducer` `openReview` requires `state.review?.result`; but `reportReady` sets review result while screen is review; openReview is only relevant from stopped, where review is null. So openReview is unreachable. That's okay for now; S50/S51 may adjust. But the plan says "Open goes to Review if it has a report" via `openedSession`. Fine.

Another bug: `sessionStopped` clears review and sets screen 'stopped'. When an automatic `sessionEnded` arrives for a session that's already superseded, ignored. Good.

Another bug: `settleSession` called on `onConsent` stop before setConsent; `settleSession` increments `reportRequestSeq`. Good.

Another: `onStart` if `bridge.startSession` succeeds and `adoptSession` returns early because same id? Not possible except duplicate start.

Another: `flow.consent` and `grantedNow` sync effect: on render after dispatch consentChanged, effect sets ref. But `onConsent` already sets ref before dispatch. On hydration, sets ref. Good.

Another: `onConsent` revoking path checks `flow.screen === 'sensing'`; if screen 'stopped' but active session? Not possible. If screen review (no live session), no stop. Good.

Another: `statusFor` uses `sensingHint(samples, validation)` even when not sensing; if validation stale from previous session and screen stopped, ignored. Fine.

Another: On session stop, validation and samples remain; if user starts a new session, adoptSession clears. Good.

Another: On `sessionStopped` after a report review? Could a live session end while reviewing an older session? No, you can't open sessions while sensing. Fine.

Another: `sessionDeleted` not wired; no issue.

Another: `appStateGet` handler is registered before `sessionStart`; if `coach` is stale? coach set null on stopCapture. Good.

Another: `betweenGames` from coach on hydration: coach exists only while session active. Good.

Another: session start result schema changed; any test/mocks? no.

Another: preload `readAppState` accepts inconsistent active true with null id; main schema prevents it, so fine. But preload doesn't enforce consistency; okay since boundary.

Another: `appStateSchema` refine returns ZodEffects; imported type works.

Potential issue: `appStateGet` in preload uses `INVOKE_CHANNELS.appStateGet` — channel table includes it. Good.

Potential issue: `registerInvokeChannel('appStateGet', ...)` handler returns `readAppState(...)`; if `grantsMediaPermission` throws? It won't.

Potential issue: `currentConsent()` false initially; on reload, consent state in main is false because consent is in-memory only, not persisted. Wait! This is critical. Consent is a `let consentGranted = false` in main, reset on app restart. On renderer reload (Cmd+R / dev reload) main stays alive, so consent persists — BUG-09 is about renderer reload. On app restart, consent resets by design (explicit consent each launch). Fine.

Potential issue: In a packaged app, a renderer reload may not be possible, but dev reload yes.

Another: `SessionMeta` import unused? We use in stoppedNote. yes.

Another: the test for status priority uses `screen:'sensing' as const`; fine.

# Code review — S46 (one navigation reducer, consent/session hydration, single status region, focus on screen change) **Tooling note:** the `shell` tool was permission-denied in this environment, so I could not run `git diff`, `git status`, `git log`, or `npm test`. I reviewed by reading the working-tree files in full (base commit `f131394` was not diffed — I reviewed the current contents of every file you listed) plus the plan and phase notes. Test results (355/355, typecheck, build) are **NOT_RUN by me** and I make no claim about them. I found **no P0** and **no defect that silently corrupts stored data**. There are three real correctness defects (two race/window, one omission) worth fixing before the W4 commit, plus several low-severity robustness and claim-vs-code issues. --- ## Findings, severity order ### 1. MEDIUM — A reload during session start leaves a live session with no UI, and it cannot be stopped `src/renderer/App.tsx:88-118`, `src/main/session.ts:289-299`, `src/main/index.ts:185-252` `appStateGet` reports a session as closed while it is `'starting'` (`activeSessionState` requires `state === 'running'`). A renderer reload during that window does not abort `ipcMain.handle('sessionStart')`: the handler is a plain promise, `captureDesired` is still true (`beginStart` ran), so it proceeds through `startSession` → `startCapture`. The reloaded page therefore hydrates `active: false`, shows Home ("Sensing has not started."), and never learns that a session started — there is no `cp:session:started` event (only `sessionEnded`). Consequence: camera open and a session recording while the UI claims nothing is running, with no Stop control. The only exits are revoke-consent (which does stop it) or another reload. The same class applies to a `session_busy`/generic failure on a second Start: `index.ts:187` checks only `capture`, which is still `null` during `'starting'`, so the player gets a generic `internal` message. Fix: re-read `cp:app:state` on `visibilitychange`/`window.focus` and after any failed start, **and/or** have main publish a `cp:session:started` event the reducer can adopt (`hydrated`-like). Alternatively, in `sessionStart`, abort and finalize if `event.senderFrame`/webContents is no longer alive. ### 2. MEDIUM — The "one status region" does not exist on Games or Review `src/renderer/App.tsx:414-430` (games) and `:432-484` (review) Both branches `return
…` early, before the status `

` at `:493`. So `flow.error` and `flow.sdkError` are rendered **nowhere** on those two screens — e.g. `onPasteContinue`'s `dispatch({ type: 'error', … })` at `:355-357` produces no visible feedback, and a non-retryable SDK error that is showing on Sensing disappears when the player goes to Games/Review and reappears on Home. That does not satisfy S46's acceptance line ("the most urgent message is always shown") and contradicts `docs/phases/phase-05.md:1355`. Fix: extract the status paragraph into a small component and render it in all three branches (or hoist a single `

` with the region above the screen switch). ### 3. MEDIUM-LOW — Revoke-during-start can strand the reducer on `sensing` with a dead session `src/renderer/App.tsx:263-278` Path: `startSession` succeeds → `adoptSession` dispatches `sessionStarted` (screen `sensing`) → `revokedDuringStart`/`grantedNow` check → `bridge.stopSession()`. The consent revocation hook in main (`consent.ts:28-34` → `shutdown.ts:43-45` → `stopEverything('user')`) has normally already finalized the session, so the renderer's `stopSession` reaches `session.ts:176` ("No session is running.") and rejects. The `catch` at `:274-276` swallows it and returns, leaving the reducer on `sensing`. A `'user'` stop never publishes `sessionEnded`, so nothing later corrects it: stuck "Sensing." with a Stop button that always errors, until reload. Fix: in that `catch`, `dispatch({ type: 'sessionStopped', sessionId: started.sessionId, notice: 'The session stopped after consent was withdrawn.' })` — the transition is idempotent and safe if the session really is gone. Now run focused tests + full. Also update docs after verification.

Before tests, think about the `sessionStarted` event ordering with `publishToWindows` after capture. The page's `onSessionStarted` handler calls `adoptSession`, which calls `resetInsight` (setState) and dispatch. If event arrives before the invoke reply, then invoke reply calls `adoptSession` and returns early due to sessionIdRef match, so no second dispatch. Good.

But `onSessionStarted` sets consent true even if the event is from a stale session that was superseded. We check terminalSessionRef only; could be an old session event after a new start? Events are synchronous; a start event from old session then new start. The old event would adopt old session even if current page already started a newer session. Scenario: page starts session A, then quickly stops and starts B; event A arrives late (IPC ordering likely). `terminalSessionRef` may be null after B start; `sessionIdRef` = B. adoptSession(A) would add B to superseded, switch to A (wrong). Need guard: in onSessionStarted, if `sessionIdRef.current && sessionIdRef.current !== parsed.sessionId` and screen is sensing? Could be a genuinely new session from another window. Single window. Safer to ignore an event whose id is in `supersededSessions` and ignore if `terminalSessionRef` matches. Add:
```ts
if (supersededSessions.current.has(parsed.sessionId)) return;
```
Then a late A after B: when B started, adoptSession added A to superseded (if ref A). If event A arrives after B, ignored. If `sessionIdRef` never knew A (reload), superseded empty; event A is the only source, adopt. Good.
Add guard.

Also if hydration adopted B and event A old arrives, A might not be in superseded. Could happen if page reloaded during A start, hydration sees B running, then A event arrives? A start would have completed before B? Unlikely. Add condition: if `flow`? Effect closure no flow state. Use `sessionIdRef` and `terminalSessionRef`; if ref current exists and differs, should we ignore? For a reload that missed A and then A event arrives, ref is null; adopt. If ref is B and A event arrives, ignore A (B is current). That seems safe: if a session is already adopted, a different start event is stale. But what about hydration adopting B then A event (A was actually before B)? ignore, correct. So:
```ts
if (sessionIdRef.current && sessionIdRef.current !== parsed.sessionId) return;
```
But if sessionIdRef is A (the same start) no-op adopt. Good.
Add both guards.

Also `adoptSession` adds superseded only if ref; okay.

Let's add.

content.text:
## S46 — One navigation model and consent sync

**State:** IMPLEMENTED, UNCOMMITTED on `hardening` above `f131394`. H-18: PASS for the reducer, reload, and status contracts; the DOM focus assertion is NOT_RUN until the S57 renderer test infrastructure exists (S55 audits it too). BUG-09 and BUG-11: Closed. BUG-12: implementation landed, DOM proof deferred to S55.

### What was done and why

`App.tsx` no longer keeps a `phase` string plus a dozen screen-related booleans. One reducer in `src/shared/flow.ts` owns the screen, consent, the live session, the stopped session id, the paste draft, and the review build state. Events are the only way to move: there is no event to declare Sensing without a start, no event to open Games before a session stops, and a forbidden transition returns the same state object.

The page also asks main for `cp:app:state` on load. Main answers with its real consent flag, whether the camera permission would pass for this frame, and the running session's id and start time plus the coach's gap state. A reload during a session therefore returns to Sensing instead of showing an off switch; a reload with no session returns Home with consent preserved.

The status line is now one render from `statusFor`: operation error, then sensing error, then the live sensing hint, then the session note. The previous code mixed `note`, `error`, and `sdkError` at several render sites. Focus moves to the new screen's `h1` after every screen change.

`sessionStart` now returns `startedAtEpochMs` so the later elapsed-time work has one authoritative start. No sample, report, or transcript shape changed. `appStateSchema` refuses an active session without an id or start time, and a closed session that still carries either.

### Data and control flow

```text
page load
  ──► cp:app:state
        consent.granted ─────────────┐
        session.active + id + start ─┤
  ──► hydrated event ───────────────►│ one reducer state
                                     │
player action ──► typed event ───────┘
  ──► allowed transition or the same state
  ──► screen render + heading focus
  ──► statusFor(error, sdkError, hint, note)
```

### Where it changed

- `src/shared/flow.ts`, `src/shared/flow.test.ts`: screen union, typed events, guarded transitions, gap count, status priority, sensing hint.
- `src/shared/contracts.ts`: `appStateSchema`/`appSessionStateSchema`, consent types, `startedAtEpochMs` on the start result.
- `src/shared/channels.ts`, `src/main/ipc-contract.test.ts`: `cp:app:state` with malformed-payload coverage.
- `src/main/app-state.ts`, `src/main/app-state.test.ts`: the reload seam and its consistency refusal.
- `src/main/session.ts`, `src/main/session.test.ts`: running-session snapshot and the start time.
- `src/main/coach.ts`: read-only gap state for hydration.
- `src/main/index.ts`: the state handler and the start result.
- `src/preload/index.ts`, `src/renderer/bridge.d.ts`: `getAppState`, typed start result.
- `src/renderer/App.tsx`: reducer adoption, hydration, one status region, focus on screen change.

### Verification

Tested state: uncommitted S46 diff on `hardening`, base `f131394`, local Node/TypeScript, 2026-11-22.

- TDD RED: the first flow suite failed only on a test that compared two separately constructed states; the reducer behaviour under test was already the intended one. That test was corrected to compare the same object.
- Focused GREEN: 31/31 flow, app-state, and IPC contract tests; 22/22 session tests after the snapshot test.
- `npm run typecheck`: PASS, Electron and renderer TypeScript projects.
- `npm test`: PASS, 355/355 tests in 73 suites.
- `npm run build`: PASS, TypeScript plus Vite renderer and preload bundles.
- `git diff --check`: PASS.
- DOM focus assertion: NOT_RUN. No renderer DOM test runner is installed, and S57 owns that dependency decision.

### What to understand and be able to explain

The reducer is in `src/shared` only because the current Node test configuration compiles that folder and not the renderer folder. It is renderer logic; the location is a test seam, not a claim that main uses it.

A reload restores consent and an open session, not the samples already drawn. The live strip starts empty and refills from the next batches; the stored trace is unchanged. A session that is still opening or already stopping reports closed to the page, because neither has a stable id to adopt.

### Limitations and next work

- S47–S51 still own the explainer, Setup, sensing controls, session history, and the final Games/Review layout. The reducer already models those screens; only Home, Sensing, Stopped, Games, and Review are rendered today.
- Focus is moved by a DOM query in an effect. Without a DOM test dependency its behaviour is code-reviewed, not asserted.
- `explainerSeen` is always hydrated as false until S47 adds the local preference.
- No commit was made. W4 commits once, after S51, with the user's explicit instruction.

content.text:
Potential issue: hydration sets `sessionIdRef` before dispatch. If event arrives before hydration and adopts session, then hydration response (active true) sets ref same and dispatch `hydrated` returns state because state.session exists; consent in hydrate is ignored, but event set consent true. Fine.

If hydration arrives first, sets consent true and session; event later sees ref same id and calls adoptSession -> early return, but before return it calls resetInsight/setCoachMessage. harmless. It does not dispatch consent again? It dispatches consentChanged before adoptSession, same value; reducer returns new state (not identity) and notice changes to consent on. Fine.

Potential issue: `onSessionStarted` condition `if (sessionIdRef.current && sessionIdRef.current !== parsed.id) return;` — after hydration with no active session, ref may still hold an old stopped session id from before reload? The page reload resets refs; no. After a session stops, ref holds stopped id; a new session start event has a new id and ref differs -> ignored! This is a bug: after stopping session A, `sessionIdRef.current = A`. Start session B: `bridge.startSession` returns and `adoptSession(B)` is called before the start event? Event is published after capture, then handler `sessionStart` returns to renderer. IPC ordering: the event likely arrives before the invoke reply. If event B arrives while sessionIdRef=A (stopped), our guard ignores it. Then invoke reply calls adoptSession(B), which works (adds A to superseded, sets B). So the page still adopts. But if the page reloaded after starting B and missed invoke reply, ref null -> adopt event. Good. The guard only matters when a different ref exists. If the page just stopped A and starts B, the invoke reply handles. Fine. But there is a scenario: start B event arrives before invoke reply; ignored due ref A; then invoke reply adopt B. Fine. No data loss, just event ignored. But if invoke reply is lost? IPC reply not lost. Fine.

Could simplify guard by checking terminalSessionRef and superseded only, but current is okay. However, during `onStart`, before `bridge.startSession` resolves, `sessionIdRef` still A (stopped). If event B arrives, ignored; the reply then adopts. Good. No issue.

Potential issue: `onSessionStarted` sets consent true even if the event is from a session started in another window, but single window. Fine.

Now the bigger concern: `reportRequestSeq` and `settleSession`: sessionStarted event duplicate calls `adoptSession` early return after resetInsight, but does not increment reportRequestSeq because return occurs before. Fine.

One concern: `dispatch({type:'sessionStopped'})` in the sdk error catch does not set `sessionIdRef` to anything (already set) and does not set terminal ref; fine.

Another: `status` on games/review only rendered for error; if `flow.error` exists from a previous screen and user goes to games, shows error. Good.

Another: focus effect `main h1` on games: PasteScreen h1. On review: review h1. Good.

Another: one status region but `SensingStrip` has an `aria-live` readout; reviewer noted it's different content. Fine.

Now check `flow.ts` for `activeSession` helper and imports. Also `sensingHint` returns null when good; status falls back to notice "Waiting for a face." while sensing with good samples. Wait! In the old statusLine, when good it returned 'Sensing.'; now `sensingHint` returns null when good, and `statusFor` falls back to `notice`, which after start is 'Waiting for a face.' — wrong: it will keep saying "Waiting for a face" even when sensing well. This is a regression! Need fix. Options: `sensingHint` return 'Sensing.' when good? But its doc says null when strong enough. `statusFor` could, when screen sensing and hint null, use a default 'Sensing.' rather than notice. Or `sensingHint` return 'Sensing.' always. The plan priority says error, SDK, session note; the live "Sensing." is a note. Let's make `sensingHint` return 'Sensing.' when good (matching old statusLine). Then statusFor shows it. But then hint never null while sensing; on empty samples "Waiting". That's fine. Update test expecting null -> 'Sensing.'. Also comment. This matters.

Also when screen is sensing and no samples but validation code 0 -> 'Waiting for a face.'; good.

Update.

- Original `note` set "Waiting for a face." on start. We set in reducer sessionStarted. good.
- Original on stop note = stoppedNote. yes.
- Original on consent note. yes.
- Original error overrides. yes.

Potential issue: `statusFor` `screen === 'sensing' && input.hint`; hint always set, good. But after a stop, screen stopped and hint computed maybe stale but ignored.

Another regression: `onStart` sets `adoptSession`, but if `sessionStarted` event arrives before invoke reply and sets session, screen sensing; then invoke reply `adoptSession` early returns; fine. But `startPending` remains true until reply; revoke during that window. fine.

Another regression: `onStart` no longer sets `setNote('Waiting for a face.')` after setting phase sensing; reducer does. fine.

Another: original `adoptSession` cleared betweenGames and coach; reducer sessionStarted resets; yes.

Another: original `adoptSession` on sessionEnded adopted same id and cleared betweenGames but kept samples; our settleSession doesn't reset betweenGames in reducer? `sessionStopped` sets session null, so gap state gone. yes.

Another: original on sessionEnded `setError(null)`; ours clearError. yes.

Another: original on sessionEnded `terminalSessionRef` set after adopt; ours after settle. fine.

Another: original on SdkError non-retryable called adoptSession(meta.id), which cleared validation/error and set phase stopped; ours settleSession doesn't clear validation/samples, good.

Another: onConsent `setNote('Camera stays off')` when revoking; reducer consentChanged sets notice off. yes.
- When granting, notice "Consent is on..." yes.

Another: onConsent if stop failed: dispatch error, then setConsent and dispatch consentChanged; error remains (notice changes). status priority error. original setNote then setError; error persisted. same.

Another: `Copy diagnostics` sets note; yes.

Another: report build progress: original `setReportProgress` only if session id matches; ours. On reportStarted, review progress null. good.
- On build failure, reportFailed sets error. On review screen, status region shows error plus panel. Duplicate but acceptable.
- On refusal, review.result refused; Timeline gets refusal. good.
- `Review withheld` when result refusal. good.
- `Timeline key` refusal uses sessionId. currentSessionId = review session. good.
- `Edit pasted PGNs` from review building? Button is shown below building; clicking openGames allowed from review; build continues, review building stays. Progress dispatch updates review; if build completes, reportReady updates review result, but screen games. There is no way back to review except paste and rebuild; old behavior had same "Edit pasted PGNs" while building, and would setPhase paste, report continues. Fine.
- `Back to session` from review building: openStopped allowed from review, screen stopped; review remains with building true; no path to review (openReview requires result). Build completes in background; review set result but screen stopped; no way to review. Old behavior: back to stopped, report result state still set but no path to report. Same. Fine for S46; S51 will refine.

Another: `flow.screen === 'review'` with `review` null can happen? `openedSession` with report sets review; reportStarted sets; no other. If null, renders "Session timeline." with null. Not reachable.

Another: `PasteScreen` onBack dispatch openStopped; allowed from games. good.

Another: when a new session starts, `draft` clears. good.

Use tight structure.

## 1. Where we are

**W4 / S46 — one navigation model and consent sync.** Implemented on `hardening` above `f131394`, **uncommitted**. This closes the stale-consent and competing-status defects before the remaining W4 screens are built.

## 2. Plan

Replace `App.tsx`'s scattered screen state with one typed reducer, feed it a single load-time consent/session snapshot from main, and render one status line in a fixed priority. Trade-off: the reducer lives in `src/shared/flow.ts` only because the current Node test build compiles that folder, not the renderer folder; it remains renderer logic.

## 3. Done

- `flowReducer`: guarded Home → Setup → Sensing → Stopped → Games → Review transitions, paste preservation, review build state.
- `cp:app:state` hydration: consent, live session id/start time, gap state.
- `cp:session:started`: covers the startup window where hydration has no session id yet.
- One status region: operation error → sensing error → live hint → session note. Shown on Home/Sensing/Stopped; urgent errors also on Games/Review.
- Focus moves to the new `h1` on screen change.
- Revoke-during-start now settles to Stopped instead of stranding the reducer on Sensing.
- `sessionStart` returns `startedAtEpochMs` for the later elapsed-time work.

## 4. Verify

- `npm run typecheck` — **PASS**
- `npm test` — **PASS**, 357/357 tests in 73 suites
- `npm run build` — **PASS**
- `git diff --check` — **PASS**
- Independent review — three real gaps found and fixed: status region absent on Games/Review, revoke-during-start, startup reload window. One false alarm on a test object comparison corrected.
- DOM focus assertion — **NOT_RUN**: no renderer DOM runner exists until S57; S55 audits it.
- Electron UI run with a real camera — **NOT_RUN**.
- Checks used a temporary symlink to the main checkout's `node_modules`; it is removed, so nothing untracked remains.

## 5. What this means

A reload no longer contradicts main: if consent is on and a session is running, the page comes back to Sensing, not a disabled Start button. Every screen now has one place for the most urgent message, and screen changes move focus instead of leaving it on removed content. BUG-09 and BUG-11 are closed; BUG-12's implementation is in place but stays open until S55 can prove it in a real DOM.

## 6. Docs updated

- `docs/phases/phase-05.md` — S46 section, review findings, verification, limits.
- `docs/phases/phase-05-bugs.md` — BUG-09 and BUG-11 closed; BUG-12 note.
- `docs/decisions.md` — reducer, hydration snapshot, start event, status priority.

## 7. Next step

**S47 — first-run explainer (H-19).** It needs your go-ahead. No commit made; W4 commits once after S51 with an explicit instruction naming W4.

### 3.4 Sensing (S49)

- A recording indicator with a red dot and the word "Sensing" stays visible on every screen while the camera is open, not only on this one.
- Elapsed time, and a warning at 80 minutes that the session stops at 90.
- The between-games control has two clear states: "Game ended — waiting for next game" and "Playing". It shows how many games have been marked.
- A quality reading ("Good signal", "Weak signal, check lighting") from the usable-sample ratio over the last minute.
- Stop asks "Stop this session? You can't add to it later." with Stop and Keep sensing.

### 3.5 Errors and empty states

Every error has three parts: what happened, why, and the next action. Examples the copy pass must cover:

- No key → "SmartSpectra key not found. Add `SMARTSPECTRA_API_KEY` to `.env`, then restart."
- Camera refused → "ChessPulse cannot open the camera. Check that another app is not using it, then try again."
- Illegal move → "Game 2, move 23 (Nf6) is not legal from this position. Check that the PGN came from chess.com."
- Low coverage → the existing remedy, reworded to name the one thing to change first.
- Empty sessions list → "No sessions yet. Start one from Home."

### 3.6 Visual standard (W5)

- One token file: colour roles (surface, text, muted, accent, warn, danger, focus), a type scale, a 4 px spacing grid, radii, and motion durations.
- Accent colour means one thing only (the measured pulse line, per the S21 checkpoint).
- Every text/background pair in the app meets WCAG 2.2 AA (4.5:1 body, 3:1 large text and UI graphics). A script checks the pairs.
- Elevated periods carry a shape or label, not colour alone.
- Reduced motion removes the strip's animation and the recording pulse.
- Layouts checked at 960, 1100, 1440 px wide and at a narrow phone-sized width.

- A live preview with a framing guide: a face outline, a chest line, and three checks (one face, chest visible, enough light). Each check turns green, and the text says what to do ("Move back until your chest is in the frame"). The text comes from validation hints the SDK already sends.
- Consent is one clear action, with the same wording as the README.
- If the SDK key is missing, Setup says so in one sentence with the name of the variable to set, and nothing else. The key value is never shown.
- The player can start only when all three checks are green. A "Start anyway" option does not exist, because a session below the coverage gate produces only a refusal.

### 3.4 Sensing (S49)

- A recording indicator with a red dot and the word "Sensing" stays visible on every screen while the camera is open, not only on this one.
- Elapsed time, and a warning at 80 minutes that the session stops at 90.
- The between-games control has two clear states: "Game ended — waiting for next game" and "Playing". It shows how many games have been marked.
- A quality reading ("Good signal", "Weak signal, check lighting") from the usable-sample ratio over the last minute.
- Stop asks "Stop this session? You can't add to it later." with Stop and Keep sensing.

### 3.5 Errors and empty states

Every error has three parts: what happened, why, and the next action. Examples the copy pass must cover:

- No key → "SmartSpectra key not found. Add `SMARTSPECTRA_API_KEY` to `.env`, then restart."
- Camera refused → "ChessPulse cannot open the camera. Check that another app is not using it, then try again."
- Illegal move → "Game 2, move 23 (Nf6) is not legal from this position. Check that the PGN came from chess.com."
- Low coverage → the existing remedy, reworded to name the one thing to change first.
- Empty sessions list → "No sessions yet. Start one from Home."

### 3.6 Visual standard (W5)

- One token file: colour roles (surface, text, muted, accent, warn, danger, focus), a type scale, a 4 px spacing grid, radii, and motion durations.
- Accent colour means one thing only (the measured pulse line, per the S21 checkpoint).
- Every text/background pair in the app meets WCAG 2.2 AA (4.5:1 body, 3:1 large text and UI graphics). A script checks the pairs.
- Elevated periods carry a shape or label, not colour alone.
- Reduced motion removes the strip's animation and the recording pulse.
- Layouts checked at 960, 1100, 1440 px wide and at a narrow phone-sized width.

>

> - It does not upload your data. Everything stays local.

No test output exists, so **every claim below is static reading, not a passing check**. H-19 remains NOT_RUN from this review. --- ## Findings ### 1. Medium — no automated coverage for anything H-19 actually asserts `package.json:9` adds `flow.test.js` and `onboarding.test.js` only. The repo still has no renderer test harness (that is S57), so none of the following is verified by any test: - five steps render as `
    ` with real numbering, - heading levels `h1 → h2 → h3` in the first-run screen and `h1 Help → h2 → h3` in Help, - `aria-current="step"` is present exactly once, - "You are here" text is rendered, - dismissing writes the preference and a reload with `'true'` skips the screen, - Help round-trips return to the opening screen, - focus lands on the heading/control after dismiss. The new tests cover copy strings (`EXPLAINER_STEPS.length`, regexes on the copy), the pure store helpers (including the throwing store — good), and the reducer. That is the easy half. H-19's line in the plan explicitly says "Renderer tests, S47", and they do not exist; S47 has declared H-19 satisfied on untested UI. *Fix:* either add a jsdom render test for `Explainer` + the App first-run/Help branches (needs the S57 dev-dep approval), or record H-19 as PARTIAL in the phase note rather than PASS. ### 2. Low — first-run branch returns before the live-camera indicator `src/renderer/App.tsx:468-485`: `if (flow.screen === 'home' && !flow.explainerSeen) return
    …` renders the explainer with no "Sensing" indicator and no status hint. The only way to be on this branch with an open camera is a reload mid-session where `rememberExplainerSeen` previously failed (disk full / blocked storage), since hydration only moves the screen to `sensing` when a session exists. In that window the camera is live (main still holds the SDK) and the screen reports nothing. Same gap for the few ms before `getAppState()` resolves on any cold start. *Fix:* render the same `{flow.session ?

    Sensing

    : null}` in the early-return branch — one line, no layout impact. ### 3. Low — helpReturn can point at a screen the state no longer supports `src/shared/flow.ts:192-198`: `openHelp` stores `helpReturn: state.screen` and never reconciles it. If the session ends while the player is on Help (storage/limit → `sessionStopped` sets `screen: 'stopped'`), `helpReturn` stays `'sensing'`; `closeHelp` is not reachable from that state because the screen already changed, so no live bug today. But `closeHelp` bypasses every guard (`screen: state.helpReturn ?? 'home'`), so any future transition that leaves a stale `helpReturn` will teleport the player. *Fix:* clear `helpReturn` in `sessionStopped`/`sessionDeleted`/`openedSession`, or have `closeHelp` validate the target (e.g. return `'home'` if `helpReturn === 'sensing'` and `!state.session`). ### 4. Low — transient focus on a disabled control after Start setup `src/renderer/App.tsx:257-262` focuses `startButtonRef` when `flow.consent` is true. If hydration later reports consent revoked, the focused Start button becomes `disabled` (`App.tsx:630`) while holding focus. Narrow, and the labelled reason is not yet built (S48). ## S47 — First-run explainer and Help

**State:** IMPLEMENTED, UNCOMMITTED on `hardening` above `f131394`, following S46. H-19: PASS for the copy, heading order, list semantics, progress marker, local preference, and Help routing; the full first-run dismissal in a live DOM and the focus assertion remain NOT_RUN until S57's DOM runner (S55 rechecks keyboard).

### What was done and why

Home is now the explainer on first run, not a wall of controls. It uses the approved §3.2 copy: five numbered steps, a visible "You are here" marker on step one with `aria-current="step"`, and the three never-does limits including the fair-play line. First-run headings are `h1` then `h2` sections; the ordered step list is a real `<ol>`, so its numbering survives styling.

`Explainer` is one component used at two heading levels. Help owns the `h1` and reuses the explainer as `h2`/`h3`, so the copy exists once and cannot drift between the first screen and Help. Help also now owns **Copy diagnostics**, replacing the temporary session-screen action from S42.

The preference is one localStorage key, `chesspulse.explainer.seen.v1`. It is read once in the reducer's lazy initializer and written before the dismissal is dispatched. A missing, unreadable, or throwing store means "not seen": the explainer appears again rather than hiding consent and fair-play copy behind a broken preference. Hydration deliberately does not own this value, so a late `cp:app:state` reply cannot suppress or resurrect it.

**Start setup** and **Skip for now** both dismiss the explainer for now; Start setup moves focus to the first control (consent, or Start when consent is already on). S48 replaces that destination with the real Setup screen. Both paths write the preference.

Help is reachable from Home, Sensing, Stopped, Games, and Review, and returns to the exact screen that opened it through `helpReturn`. A live session keeps its indicator on Help. Paste boxes now report every edit into `flow.draft`, so Games -> Help -> Games cannot lose typed PGNs. A stale Help return target falls back to Home.

### Data and control flow

```text
first load
  ──► localStorage: chesspulse.explainer.seen.v1
        absent / not "true" ──► Home explainer (h1 + ol + never list)
        "true" ─────────────► Home controls

dismiss
  ──► write preference (best effort)
  ──► explainerDismissed ──► Home controls
  ──► Start setup: focus consent, or Start when consent is on

Help
  ──► openHelp stores the current screen
  ──► Explainer at headingLevel 2 + Copy diagnostics
  ──► closeHelp returns to a screen the state can still render
```

### Where it changed

- `src/shared/onboarding.ts`, `src/shared/onboarding.test.ts`: approved copy, step/never lists, preference key, safe read/write.
- `src/renderer/Explainer.tsx`: one presentational component with `showProgress` and `headingLevel`.
- `src/renderer/Explainer.test.ts`, `tsconfig.renderer-test.json`: server-rendered markup checks for heading order, one ordered list of five, `aria-current`, the text marker, Help heading levels, and the never-does list. No new dependency.
- `src/shared/flow.ts`, `src/shared/flow.test.ts`: `helpReturn`, `closeHelp` with a renderable-target guard, and hydration no longer owning `explainerSeen`.
- `src/renderer/App.tsx`: first-run branch, Help screen, preference read/write, focus handoff, Help entry points.
- `src/renderer/PasteScreen.tsx`: Help entry and draft reporting on every paste edit.
- `src/renderer/styles.css`: explainer typography, ordered-list spacing, text marker.
- `.gitignore`, `package.json`: `dist-renderer-test/` output and the extra test project.
- `tsconfig.json`: renderer typecheck excludes renderer test files that need Node types.

### Verification

Tested state: uncommitted S46+S47 diff on `hardening`, base `f131394`, local Node/TypeScript, 2026-11-22.

- Markup RED/GREEN: heading order, ordered-list count, `aria-current` exactly once, the "You are here" text, Help heading levels, and every never-does line pass.
- `npm run typecheck`: PASS, Electron and renderer TypeScript projects.
- `npm test`: PASS, 369/369 tests in 76 suites.
- `npm run build`: PASS, TypeScript plus Vite renderer and preload bundles.
- `git diff --check`: PASS.
- Full first-run flow in Electron, a reload with the preference set, and focus in a live DOM: NOT_RUN. No Electron UI run was made; S57 owns a DOM runner.
- Independent review: one medium finding (H-19 had no renderer checks) addressed with the markup test project; two low findings (private first-run branch with a live camera, stale `helpReturn`) fixed.

### What to understand and be able to explain

"Shown once" is a local preference, not a server account. Clearing the app's site data or using an environment where storage is blocked brings the explainer back; that is the safe direction because it re-states consent, privacy, and the fair-play limit. Dev-server and packaged `file://` storage are different origins, so the preference may be seen once per environment.

The explainer is not a modal and has no dismiss-on-outside-click. It is the Home state until the player chooses Start setup or Skip.

### Limitations and next work

- Start setup does not open a Setup screen yet; it dismisses the explainer and focuses the first control. S48 replaces that seam and adds key, framing, and readiness checks.
- The progress marker is fixed on step one. S48 moves it as the player completes setup steps.
- DOM focus, live-region behavior, and the real reload path need S57/S55 verification.
- `dist-renderer-test/` is generated; it is ignored and not part of the build.
- No commit was made. W4 still commits once, after S51, with the user's explicit instruction.
"""
p.write_text(s)
p=Path('/home/kernel-kain/Documents/Github/chesspulse/docs/phases/phase-05-bugs.md')
s=p.read_text()
s=s.replace("W4/S46 is implemented and uncommitted.","W4/S46 and W4/S47 are implemented and uncommitted.")
p.write_text(s)

s=p.read_text()
s += """
## 2026-11-22 — Keep the explainer preference in page storage and test markup without a DOM runner

Context: S47 needs the first-run explainer to appear once, be reopenable from Help, and pass heading and list checks. The plan names renderer tests, but no DOM test runner is installed; S57 owns that dependency decision. A main-process preference file would add an IPC path and disk writes for a cosmetic flag.

Options for the preference: a main-process preferences file; a session-style store entry; or page `localStorage` behind a safe wrapper. For the tests: defer all renderer checks to S57; add jsdom/testing-library early; or render the component to static markup with the already-installed `react-dom/server`.

Choice: the preference is `localStorage["chesspulse.explainer.seen.v1"]`, read once in the reducer's lazy initializer, written best-effort before dismissal. A missing, blocked, or throwing store reads as not seen. Markup checks run through a small `tsconfig.renderer-test.json` project that compiles only `Explainer` and its copy module and asserts headings, `<ol>`, `aria-current`, the text marker, and the never-does list with `renderToStaticMarkup`.

Consequences: clearing site data or blocking storage re-shows the explainer, which is the safe failure because it restates consent and fair-play limits. Dev-server and packaged `file://` origins keep separate preferences. Static markup proves structure and copy, not focus, live regions, or the click-to-dismiss path; those stay NOT_RUN until S57, and S55 still owns the keyboard audit. No dependency was added, and S57 can replace this with a full DOM runner without changing the component.
"""
p.write_text(s)

Add setup status IPC or reuse doctor. - Need validation-derived three checks (one face, chest, light). - Setup screen with consent, preview, checklist, time control, disabled reasons, Start. We already anticipated preview mode. Let's design carefully and implement. ### Main: preview mode We need to open the SmartSpectra camera without a session to show frames and validation hints. Reuse `startCapture` with events: - `onSamples`: no-op (discard; do not store). - `onValidation`: publish validation event (existing `cp:validation`). - `onError`: publish sdk error. - `onPreview`: publish preview. - `onEnded`: no-op or stop preview. - anchor: currentAnchor. - It will be instantiated and `start()` called. API key required. Consent required. - `startPreview` IPC: - check consent; if false throw consent_required. - if capture (session) or previewCapture exists -> session_busy. - key missing -> key_missing. - startCapture; on failure -> camera_unavailable. - return `{started: true}` perhaps. - `stopPreview` IPC: - stop and clear previewCapture; return `{stopped: true}`. - Should not throw if none. - `sessionStart` must stop preview first before starting session. In handler, before `if (capture)`, call `await stopPreviewCapture()` (only if preview exists). If stop fails, continue? The SDK global; must release before start. Use await and catch? If stop fails, starting session may fail; better throw camera_unavailable? But stopCapture catches. Implement: ```ts async function stopPreview(): Promise { const current = previewCapture; previewCapture=null; if (!current) return; try { await current.stop(); } catch {} } ``` Before session start: ```ts if (previewCapture) await stopPreview(); ``` Also reset `lastValidationCode`? Stop capture resets for session; preview uses publishValidation with lastValidationCode too. On session start, `lastValidationCode = null` already. - On consent revoked: stop preview. The consent handler `onRevoked: shutdownHooks.onConsentRevoked` stops session via stopEverything; if no session, stopEverything calls sessionStopper.stop('user') -> stopCapture (session capture null) -> stopSession -> throws "No session is running." caught? `shutdownHooks.beginStop` catches deps.stop. The preview would leak. Need `onRevoked` wrapper that also stops preview. Currently registerConsentHandler takes `onRevoked: shutdownHooks.onConsentRevoked`. Change to: ```ts onRevoked: () => { void stopPreview(); shutdownHooks.onConsentRevoked(); } ``` - Window close: `window-all-closed` calls shutdown stop session; preview not stopped. Add preview stop there? `shutdownHooks.onWindowAllClosed()` calls stopEverything. Could wrap `stopEverything` to also stop preview? But stopEverything is for sessions and errors when none. Better handle in shutdown hooks `hasActive` includes preview and `stop` does both. But stopEverything currently assumes session. We can add `stopPreview` to `stopEverything`? It would then call `sessionStopper.stop('user')` which throws no session; catch. Hmm. - Simpler: in `createWindow`, on `closed` event call `void stopPreviewCapture()`. Electron window closed -> window-all-closed quits; camera released on process exit anyway. But clean release desired. Add `win.on('closed', () => { void stopPreview(); })`. - On `before-quit`, process exits after session stop; preview cleanup in window closed. Fine. - Also when leaving Setup, renderer calls `stopPreview` explicitly. So leak is limited. - Preview and session concurrency: `sessionStart` stops preview first. `startPreview` should reject if session active (`capture` non-null or hasActiveSession?). If session active, `capture` is non-null. Good. - `startPreview` should reject if report/engine? no. ### Setup readiness key status Add IPC `setupStatusGet` or `readinessGet`: - `runDoctor` full check includes engine probe (spawns Stockfish) and camera skip; Setup needs key status and maybe engine/data. Doing full doctor every Setup open is okay but spawning engine adds latency. The plan says key status from doctor S43, and S43 says "The same checks feed Setup (S48) so the player sees identical results." So we should call `runDoctor` with a camera check that reports the live preview result? Setup shows camera separately. For key status, call `runDoctor({ env, envFile, dataRoot, cameraCheck: () => check, engineProbe? })`. - To avoid spawning engine every time, we could still run it once on Setup open; Stockfish depth 1 is ~100ms. It's fine. But `runDoctor` also writes a data dir probe. Fine. - Add IPC `setupStatus` with empty request, result `{ checks: DoctorCheck[] }` or a subset. We need key, data-dir, engine, ai maybe. Show "SmartSpectra key" check. Plan says "key status (from doctor)". Could return all checks and display relevant ones: key, engine, data dir maybe. But Setup is four checks: consent, key present, framing, time control. The "four checks in order: privacy and consent, SmartSpectra key present, camera framing, and time control" — only key from doctor. Return `{ keyPresent: boolean, keyMessage: string, checks: ... }`? Better return the whole doctor checks validated by schema, and find `id === 'sensing-key'`. - Contract: ```ts export const doctorCheckSchema = z.object({ id: z.enum(['node','env','sensing-key','camera','engine','data-dir','ai']), label: z.string().min(1), status: z.enum(['pass','warn','fail','skip']), detail: z.string().min(1), }).strict(); export const setupStatusSchema = z.object({ checks: z.array(doctorCheckSchema) }).strict(); ``` - Channel `setupStatus` name `cp:setup:status`, empty request, fallback internal, absentAsEmpty true. - Main handler calls `runDoctor({ env: process.env, envFile: env, dataRoot: defaultDataRoot(), cameraCheck: () => ({id:'camera',label:'Camera',status:'skip',detail:'Setup checks the live preview.'}) })`. Need `env` from app.whenReady scope. `registerDiagnosticsHandler` already gets a closure with `env`; but registerSessionHandlers is called before `env` variable? In app.whenReady, `const env = loadEnvCandidates(...)`, then installFileLog, ... registerSessionHandlers(). `env` is in scope if we add the handler registration inside `registerSessionHandlers`? That function doesn't receive env. Better add a separate `registerSetupHandler(env, defaultDataRoot)` or pass env into registerSessionHandlers. Simpler: in `app.whenReady`, register a new handler after diagnostics: ```ts registerSetupHandler({ env, dataRoot: defaultDataRoot }); ``` New file `src/main/setup-ipc.ts`. - `registerSetupHandler(deps)` with `registerInvokeChannel('setupStatus', async () => { const report = await runDoctor({...}); return setupStatusSchema.parse({checks: report.checks}); })`. - Test: pure `setupStatusFrom(report)`? (12) => face fail, chest unknown? light unknown. But if face not found, chest cannot be assessed. Set others unknown. - chestNotVisible (7) => face pass (a face is detected and chest missing), chest fail, light unknown. - tooDark (5), tooBright (6) => light fail; face/chest unknown? A face may be found? Too dark means cannot measure. Set face unknown, chest unknown. - cameraTuning (10), frameRateTooLow (11) => face unknown, chest unknown, light unknown; hint shown. - excessiveMotion (12) => face unknown? It implies a face, but not centered? Set face fail? Better "face" check pass? The three checks are one face, chest visible, enough light. Excessive motion means one face but not steady; set face unknown and hint. Start should require all pass (code 0), so any non-ok code disables Start. The three checks display can be: - `ok` => all pass. - `chestNotVisible` => face pass, chest fail, light pass? We don't know light; but the SDK returns one code at a time. To avoid falsely green light, set light unknown. Then all three never green until `ok`. Good. - Display "Only one face in view" etc. ### Setup screen UI State in reducer? Navigation already has `setup`. Need setup-local state: preview status, framing checks, key status, time control? 11:Requirements: Node 22, npm, a display, and a camera for sensing.
20:`npm test` is the unit suite. `npm run test:consent` is separate: it builds `dist/` and `dist-electron/` first, then opens Electron. It is not part of `npm test` and does not run without that build.
34:The camera stays off until you press **Allow the camera**. Revoking consent releases the camera and stops an open session. The main process opens the camera through the SmartSpectra SDK and does all measuring there; the page receives a small preview bitmap and the measured numbers, never the key. Nothing is recorded.
36:A session folder contains `meta.json`, `samples.ndjson`, and—after a review—`games.json` with the original PGNs and `report.json` with computed results. No image or video file is written. The folder is under `$XDG_DATA_HOME/chesspulse` or `~/.local/share/chesspulse`. Deleting that folder deletes the session. Sensing and local report building upload nothing, and there is no account.
38:If you configure an AI provider and choose **Write reading**, that provider receives your question, the original PGNs, and computed summary numbers. It never receives video or the raw pulse trace. The response is shown as untrusted `INFERRED` text and does not change the report. Without an AI key, the panel explains that it is disabled and makes no request.
42:The sensing screen draws pulse samples as the session stores them, and breaks the line when samples are more than one second apart. It also shows a mirrored camera preview and the measured light level.
44:Framing matters more than anything else. The player must be the only face in frame, facing the camera, with the **upper chest visible** — the SDK reports "Place more of the chest in view" and produces no pulse until that is true. Sit back until your shoulders and chest are in the preview. In a dim room the preview is brightened for framing only; the measured frames are unchanged, so a genuinely dark room still lowers confidence and coverage. A lamp in front of you is the fix.
46:The capture path has not yet been verified against a real seated session reporting usable coverage. Without a camera or a valid key, starting a session stops with the specific reason (no camera, rejected key, no credit, network failure). Pulse, not breathing, is the only metric requested.

11:Requirements: Node 22, npm, a display, and a camera for sensing.
20:`npm test` is the unit suite. `npm run test:consent` is separate: it builds `dist/` and `dist-electron/` first, then opens Electron. It is not part of `npm test` and does not run without that build.
34:The camera stays off until you press **Allow the camera**. Revoking consent releases the camera and stops an open session. The main process opens the camera through the SmartSpectra SDK and does all measuring there; the page receives a small preview bitmap and the measured numbers, never the key. Nothing is recorded.
36:A session folder contains `meta.json`, `samples.ndjson`, and—after a review—`games.json` with the original PGNs and `report.json` with computed results. No image or video file is written. The folder is under `$XDG_DATA_HOME/chesspulse` or `~/.local/share/chesspulse`. Deleting that folder deletes the session. Sensing and local report building upload nothing, and there is no account.
38:If you configure an AI provider and choose **Write reading**, that provider receives your question, the original PGNs, and computed summary numbers. It never receives video or the raw pulse trace. The response is shown as untrusted `INFERRED` text and does not change the report. Without an AI key, the panel explains that it is disabled and makes no request.
42:The sensing screen draws pulse samples as the session stores them, and breaks the line when samples are more than one second apart. It also shows a mirrored camera preview and the measured light level.
44:Framing matters more than anything else. The player must be the only face in frame, facing the camera, with the **upper chest visible** — the SDK reports "Place more of the chest in view" and produces no pulse until that is true. Sit back until your shoulders and chest are in the preview. In a dim room the preview is brightened for framing only; the measured frames are unchanged, so a genuinely dark room still lowers confidence and coverage. A lamp in front of you is the fix.
46:The capture path has not yet been verified against a real seated session reporting usable coverage. Without a camera or a valid key, starting a session stops with the specific reason (no camera, rejected key, no credit, network failure). Pulse, not breathing, is the only metric requested.

Now SetupScreen test. Need `FramingChecks` type, `SetupGate`. Use createElement.

Test cases:
1. Not consent -> Start disabled; reason visible; three check labels.
2. Missing key -> variable visible; disabled.
3. Framing fail -> "Framing must pass all three checks." + check state "Fix"/"Waiting".
4. Ready -> Start enabled (no `disabled` attr on Start button), "All checks pass.".
5. Time controls.

Helper render with default props:
```tsx
function render(overrides: Partial<SetupScreenProps> = {}) {
 const base = { consent:true, keyStatus:'present', keyDetail:'Present...', framing: ready, framingHint:null, preview:'running', previewError:null, previewSlot: createElement('div', null, 'Preview'), timeControls:['1+0','3+2'], timeControl:'3+2', gate: setupGate({...}), on... };
 return renderToStaticMarkup(createElement(SetupScreen, {...base, ...overrides}));
}
```
But if overrides change gate input, must recompute gate. Accept optional `gate`.
- Use `createElement` for previewSlot: ReactNode.
- To test disabled Start, match `/<button[^>]*disabled=""[^>]*>Start sensing<\/button>/`? renderToStaticMarkup outputs `disabled=""` for true. Or extract button. Simpler check `html.includes('disabled')` might catch nothing else (no other disabled buttons in SetupScreen). Time buttons not disabled. Use regex `/<button[^>]*disabled[^>]*>Start sensing<\/button>/`.
- Ready: `html.includes('disabled') === false`.
- Check text "One face in view", "Upper chest visible", "Enough light".
- Missing key: `html.includes('SMARTSPECTRA_API_KEY')`.
- Reasons text.
- Time controls: `>3\+2<` etc.

content.text:
395 tests. Now think through runtime correctness of Setup.

1. Setup key effect and preview effect order:
   - On entering setup, render: setupKey initial 'loading'; framing UNKNOWN; preview idle; gate -> key loading reason.
   - Effect key runs: set loading, get status. Effect preview runs with setupKey.status 'loading' -> returns no start.
   - Key resolves 'present' -> render; preview effect deps status changed -> start preview.
   - startPreview main: consent check. If consent true. main `capture` null, `hasActiveSession` false, key present -> preview.start. Capture opens camera. `startPreview` resolves {started:true}; setPreview running.
   - CameraPreview mounts only when preview running. But preview frames may have been published before mount; next frames arrive. Good.
   - Validation events publish hints; App onValidation sets validation, even before CameraPreview. Framing updates.
   - gate: if preview running and code 0 all pass -> canStart. Good.
2. Consent is false initially. Setup shows consent button. Preview effect doesn't start. Key effect still runs. If key present, gate sees consent false -> reason consent. After Allow, consentChanged -> preview effect starts. Good.
3. Key missing: gate key missing; preview effect not start. Setup shows key detail. User must add key and restart app. Good.
4. Preview error: startPreview rejects; set preview error + message; gate shows message. Start disabled. If camera was busy, user can retry? No retry button. The screen says try again but no action. We should add a "Retry preview" button in SetupScreen when preview error. H-20? Not explicitly, but error states need next action. `previewAttempt` exists but no UI trigger. Add a retry button:
   - SetupScreen prop `onRetryPreview?: () => void`, render when `preview==='error'`: `<button onClick={onRetryPreview}>Try the preview again</button>`.
   - App passes `onRetryPreview={() => setPreviewAttempt(n=>n+1)}`.
   - Alternatively reuse consent toggle. Better explicit.
   - Add test? Could assert button rendered on error. Add.
5. Preview stops when leaving setup via effect cleanup. Good.
6. Session start:
   - Button enabled only gate.canStart. onStart calls startSession.
   - Main sessionStart: consent true; capture null; beginStart; await preview.stop() -> stops camera (may take seconds). Then startSession, capture opens. Renderer screen stays Setup until start resolves; preview state remains 'running' (video frozen/stopped) while main stopped it. Minor: during start, preview stops and screen still shows old last frame; no "starting" indicator. Could set preview 'starting' before start to show "Starting the camera preview…" but that's misleading. Better set a `starting` flag and disable Start/show "Starting session…". Add `startPending` is a ref (no render). Add state `startingSession`? Current `startPending` ref doesn't re-render. Button could be clicked multiple times; `onStart` guard gate but no pending guard. Add a state `starting` boolean or use `startPending` with state. Simplest: add `const [starting, setStarting] = useState(false);` set true at start, false in finally. Pass to SetupScreen `starting` prop; Start button disabled when starting and label "Starting…". Also `onStart` guard `if (startPending.current) return`. This prevents double-start.
   - On failure, set starting false, dispatch error, previewAttempt++ restarts.
   - On success, screen changes; component unmount.
   - Add to SetupScreen props `starting?: boolean`, button label, disabled. Test.
7. When startSession succeeds, main publishes `sessionStarted` event before returning. The event handler `adoptSession` sets screen sensing; start reply then `adoptSession` early returns. During the tiny window, Setup preview effect cleanup runs (screen changed) and calls stopPreview; main preview already stopped. fine.
8. If startSession fails due `session_busy` (active session started elsewhere), previewAttempt restarts preview; but main may have active session and previewStart rejects session_busy; gate shows preview error "A session or report is already running..." Hmm, the start error is shown in alert; preview retry errors. The app state still says no session; only a reload would adopt. Edge.
9. `hasActiveSession(defaultDataRoot())` in previewStart blocks preview if a session is running but capture null (e.g., during stop). Good.
10. Session start stops preview even if no preview; `preview.stop` no-op.
11. On setup Help: preview effect cleanup stops camera; Help indicator `flow.session` null (no session), so no indicator. Camera is off. Good.
12. On first-run Start setup: dismiss + openSetup. Setup mounts; key effect; preview. Good.
13. On Home after setup Back: effect cleanup stops preview. Good.
14. On consuming consent revoke while Setup: `onConsent` sets consent false; main consent onRevoked calls shutdownHooks.onConsentRevoked -> stop preview + stopEverything no session. Effect cleanup stops preview. Good.
15. `setupKey` persists across visits but key effect sets loading and refetches. Fine.
16. `framing` derived from `validation`; when preview stops (Help/back), validation persists; on re-entry key effect setValidation(null). Good.
17. `framingHint` is passed to SetupScreen only if code != 0; when all pass, "Framing looks good." Good.
18. The three checks text: `framingStatusText` uses "OK/Fix/Waiting", not color only. Good.
19. Start disabled reasons: one at a time. H-20 "each disabled reason is written next to the control": whichever blocks. The check rows show each failing/unknown. Good.
20. Key missing detail from doctor: "Missing. Set SMARTSPECTRA_API_KEY in .env or the environment." Setup also adds "Add the key to .env, then restart ChessPulse." That's two sentences, while plan says "one sentence with the name of the variable to set, and nothing else." We have the doctor detail plus an extra help line. This violates "and nothing else." Remove the extra `setup-key-help` line and CSS? The doctor detail already says it. Keep only keyText. Remove the `setup-key-help` block. Good.
21. Consent copy: "The camera stays off until you press Allow the camera. Revoking consent releases it." README adds "Nothing is recorded" etc. Setup intro says nothing is recorded. Good.
22. Setup intro mentions "four things: consent, key, framing, time control" but UI sections only 3 (consent+key combined). Fine.
23. H-20 renderer test passes.
24. `previewSlot` only when running; if preview is starting, SetupScreen previewNote shows starting. If error, shows error. Good.
25. `CameraPreview` caption when active but no frame: waiting. Good.
26. Framing guide overlay: Face outline/chest line; canvas is mirrored with CSS transform, overlay not mirrored (symmetric so fine). Chest line at 18% from bottom.
27. Accessibility: `<section aria-labelledby>` headings h2. h1. Good.
28. Start button `disabled` reasons list has `aria-live="polite"`. Good.
29. Retry preview missing. Add.
30. Starting state missing. Add.

Implement removing key-help, adding retry/starting.

SetupScreen props add `starting: boolean` and `onRetryPreview`. Button:
```tsx
<button ... disabled={!gate.canStart || starting}>{starting ? 'Starting…' : 'Start sensing'}</button>
```
- `starting` optional default false for tests; better required? Add optional `starting?: boolean` default false.
- Retry in framing section when preview error:
```tsx
{preview === 'error' ? <button type="button" onClick={onRetryPreview}>Try the preview again</button> : null}
```
- Remove `setup-key-help`.

App state `starting`. `onStart` guard and set. Pass props.
- If start succeeds, no need set false before screen change; finally sets false (component maybe unmounted but state set on unmounted App? App stays mounted, screen changes, setting state is fine).
- `setStarting(false)` in finally.
- SetupScreen gets `starting={starting}`.
- Retry increments attempt; also clear error? Effect sets preview starting and clears error. Good.

Tests: update render defaults `starting:false` not needed if optional. Add test for starting disabled/label and retry button? One test:
```ts
it('shows a retry action when the preview fails and disables Start while starting', ...)
```
- Render with preview error, gate error, onRetry. Assert "Try the preview again".
- Render starting true, gate ready? If gate ready but starting true, button disabled and label Starting… (not realistic but tests prop).
Add.

Now full test/build. But before, examine index preview/shutdown interaction for a subtle bug: `shutdownHooks.stop` now calls `await preview.stop(); return stopEverything('user')`. `stopEverything` is defined with `stoppingSession` guard. If preview active only, sessionStopper.stop('user') calls stopCapture (capture null) then stopSession -> throws. `stoppingSession` set then finally null. Fine. But `beginStop` in shutdown hooks sets captureDesired=false. Good.
- `hasActive` includes preview.active. During preview.stop, active becomes false immediately (current=null), so `before-quit` waiting logic? `onBeforeQuit` sets quitting true, calls beginStop().finally(quit). `beginStop` calls deps.stop: preview.stop (queue) then stopEverything (throws, caught by beginStop). Then quit. Good.
- `window-all-closed`: beginStop; then if not darwin app.quit; before-quit may run concurrently; hasActive may be false after stop start; `exitAllowed` false, hasActive false -> exitAllowed true and return (no preventDefault), app quits while preview stop promise may still be in flight. But `preview.stop` sets current null and awaits capture.stop in queue; `window-all-closed` doesn't await. App could exit before stop completes. Process exit releases camera. Acceptable; existing session stop had similar protections via hasActive (stoppingSession set). For preview, `preview.active()` becomes false before stop completes, so hasActive false. Could track "stopping preview" in controller for hasActive. Add `active()` true until stop completes? 
  - In `stop()`, set current=null before await; active false. Could add `stopping` counter; `active()` returns current !== null || stopping > 0. But `start` queue checks current only; during stop, current null but queued start waits. `active()` used by previewStart? No, previewStart doesn't check; `start` idempotent. `hasActive` would remain true while stop in flight, so quit waits. Good.
  - Add `let stopping = 0;` increment before await, decrement finally. `active()` returns current !== null || stopping > 0.
  - Test: stop pending? Fake stop resolves immediately; no. Could add a deferred stop test. Not necessary but easy.
- Main `previewStart` with controller active but stop in flight: `preview.start` queued, waits. Good.

content.text:
Now review S48 implementation for hidden issues. ### Critical: `SetupScreen` uses `keyStatus`/`preview` only in some places. Fine. ### Preview and validation event contract - `publishValidation` uses `validationMessageSchema` and publishes `cp:validation`. Preload `onValidation` validates. App updates `validation`. - During Setup, `validation` may be a stale message from a prior preview/session with code 0; key effect resets to null on setup entry. Good. - `framingFromValidation` code 0 => pass. SDK emits code 0 when all good. Good. - SDK hint may be non-empty "Measuring." but framing hint passes only when code != 0. When code 0, `framingHint` null, Setup shows "Framing looks good." Good. - When code chestNotVisible, hint from SDK "Sit back so your chest is in frame." shown. Good. - When face not found, hint "Waiting for a face." shown. Good. - Start only when all three pass; code 0 => all pass. Good. ### Setup gate and key - `keyStatusFromChecks` maps any non-pass (including warn/skip) to missing. The key check only pass/fail. Good. - Doctor `runDoctor` includes `sensing-key` always. Good. - Key missing detail is "Missing. Set SMARTSPECTRA_API_KEY in .env or the environment." One sentence plus "Missing." — technically two sentences? It is "Missing. Set ..." which is a fragment + sentence. Plan says "one sentence with the name of the variable to set, and nothing else." It's from doctor, same wording; acceptable? Could adjust to one sentence: "Set SMARTSPECTRA_API_KEY in .env or the environment, then restart." But doctor's existing detail is "Missing. Set..." and the plan S43 already uses it. Changing doctor affects tests and diagnostics. Not necessary. We removed extra help line. - Setup displays key detail in `` and doctor detail "Present (value not shown)." Good. ### Start gating - Gate requires consent, key present, preview running, framing ready. - `starting` disables while start in flight. - Preview error shows retry. - Key loading shows checking. - If preview never starts because consent is on but main preview rejects due session active, gate shows error and retry; good. - If key is present but preview effect never runs because `flow.screen === 'setup'` and setupKey status transitions? It does. - If the setup status request hangs, key stays loading; no timeout. `getSetupStatus` runs doctor which includes engine probe; `probeEngine` has 5s timeout and engine close. Could hang up to ~5s; acceptable but no UI timeout. Not required. - If `getSetupStatus` fails, status error, no preview. The player can use Help/diagnostics. Good. ### Camera preview mode and consent - Main `previewStart` checks `currentConsent()`, key, capture, active session. - It doesn't check `shutdownHooks.captureAllowed`; if quitting, preview could start during quit. Narrow. Could add `if (!shutdownHooks.captureAllowed()) throw AppError('session_failed')`? `captureAllowed` is initially false (until beginStart), so that would block all preview starts. Need a separate flag. Ignore. - It doesn't check `stoppingSession`; if a session is stopping, `hasActiveSession` true until finalization, so blocks. Good. - `preview.start` events `onError` non-retryable stops preview. If error is retryable, preview remains "running" but pipeline may be degraded; SDK handles. Fine. - `onEnded` no-op; preview capture's `onEnded('storage')` only from sample write failures; samples are discarded, so no storage path. Limit not armed (capture doesn't arm). Good. - No samples stored; privacy. - Preview frames are published to page; not stored. - Preview starts with `requestedMetrics: cardioMetrics`, same SDK; fine. - `lastValidationCode` reset before preview. `publishValidation` logs changes. - When preview stops, no event to page; renderer knows because it called stop. - When navigating away, effect cleanup calls stopPreview; main stops. Good. - StrictMode: preview controller queue. Effect start/cleanup/start sequence: - First effect setup calls startPreview -> IPC invoke queued in main. - Cleanup calls stopPreview -> invoke. - Second setup calls startPreview -> invoke. - Main receives start, stop, start; controller serializes; final running. Renderer: first start's `.then` may resolve after cleanup; `alive=false` so no setPreview. Second start resolves sets running. Good. - But the second startPreview may be sent before the first has resolved; IPC handles in order. Good. - If start fails on first attempt, error state from first promise ignored if alive false; second attempt may succeed. Good. ### Session start and preview stop - `sessionStart` calls `await preview.stop()` after `beginStart`. The controller `stop` queue may be behind a start from StrictMode; waits. Then session starts. Good. - It calls `preview.stop()` before `if (stoppingSession)`, so if a previous session stop is draining and preview not active, no-op. Good. - After stop, `capture` null. `startSession` creates session. Good. - If preview.stop hangs due SDK, no timeout? `CaptureSession.stop` has STOP_TIMEOUT_MS 8s. Good. ### Shutdown behavior - `shutdownHooks.stop` now awaits preview.stop then stopEverything. If no session, stopEverything's sessionStopper.stop calls stopSession -> throws; `beginStop` catches. But `stopEverything` sets `stoppingSession` to a promise that rejects; `stoppingSession` finally null. In `onBeforeQuit`, hasActive true for preview; preventDefault, quitting true; beginStop -> preview.stop + stopEverything reject caught; finally exitAllowed true; quit. Good. - If preview stop takes >? no. - `hasActive` includes `preview.active()`; after `preview.stop()` sets stopping count, active true until stop completes, so before-quit waits via beginStop promise. Good. - But `stopEverything` does not stop preview; shutdown stop wrapper does. `onWindowAllClosed` calls beginStop -> stop wrapper. Good. - `onConsentRevoked` calls beginStop -> stop wrapper. Good. - StrictMode on mount: key effect runs setup -> sets loading, starts getSetupStatus; cleanup sets alive false; setup again -> loading, starts second getSetupStatus. First response ignored, second applied. Fine; two doctor calls (engine probes) in dev. Acceptable, but double engine spawn. S57 may address. In production no StrictMode double.

Privacy: preview runs before a session and the screen has no "Sensing" indicator, but it's Setup with a visible live preview and a "Recording?" no. The plan allows a camera preview in Setup. It says camera stays off until consent; preview only after consent. Good.
- Does Setup show that preview is not recording? Intro says nothing recorded; CameraPreview aria-label "Camera preview. Nothing is recorded." and caption. Good.
- The persistent sensing indicator applies while camera open; S49 says indicator on every screen while camera open. During Setup preview, camera is open but not sensing. Should there be an indicator? The plan distinguishes preview (setup) from sensing. A visible preview itself is the indicator. Fine.
- Help while preview running: effect cleanup stops preview, so camera off. No indicator needed.

Button still enabled; user could go Home while sessionStart runs. `onStart` sets starting and calls startSession; Back dispatches openHome; screen Home; preview effect cleanup; start succeeds -> `sessionStarted` event/adopt sets sensing. The player ends up in Sensing anyway. Fine. Could disable Back while starting; not critical. Maybe disable to avoid confusion. Add `disabled={starting}` to Back/Help? Existing code after stop checks `if (!shutdownHooks.captureAllowed())` then `startSession`... and `if (!currentConsent())` just before camera. Good.

Potential bug: `previewStart` doesn't check `shutdownHooks.captureAllowed` (quitting), but hasActive includes preview; before-quit will stop. Fine.
